### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**2** anchor(s) derived from **2** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **31** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 90637274875768a63f274895a4c6b4c9949ba1af` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `b03a2014529a3b410578d2192747012745795cac` — the merge of head `33934882f849b1fcdd311113e73f86a3b1fb964f` into base `90637274875768a63f274895a4c6b4c9949ba1af`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin b03a2014529a3b410578d2192747012745795cac && git checkout b03a2014529a3b410578d2192747012745795cac
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 90637274875768a63f274895a4c6b4c9949ba1af 33934882f849b1fcdd311113e73f86a3b1fb964f && git checkout -B drift-repro 90637274875768a63f274895a4c6b4c9949ba1af && git merge --no-ff 33934882f849b1fcdd311113e73f86a3b1fb964f

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 90637274875768a63f274895a4c6b4c9949ba1af
```

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `33934882f849b1fcdd311113e73f86a3b1fb964f`
Local-runs: none

Inputs read: card #23372 (body and all four comments: triage, regrade, claim, os-dev-report), PR #23471 (body, file list, net diff against `main` from merge-base `7b3d5585`), and the check-runs on the head. The branch's three commits and the two probe files, the service's own resolve gate, the audience contract, the error-code ledger, the ADR register, the QA checklist and the Clause-② rule text were read at the head to judge the diff; nothing was built, run or re-run. This is a `security` card in `domain:services`: evidence below is described abstractly, with no reproduction recipe.

### ① Derived judgments

Accept set (requests the public resolve door serves), both mounts:

- **Unchanged — right.** The service's resolve gate is untouched; the new arm runs only inside the branch where the service has already refused. The one served cell (an allowlisted email claim together with the correct password; on a password-less link, the allowlisted claim alone) is pinned at 200 on both mounts, anonymous and signed in.

Public surface (which refusal a refused caller reads), both mounts:

- **A live `email`-audience link that did not resolve now answers the probe's existing generic refusal, `404 INVALID_OR_EXPIRED`, for every refused cell — right.** Before, when the link also carried a password, those cells read `401 NEEDS_PASSWORD` / `401 WRONG_PASSWORD` from the password arm, which knows only whether a password was sent, so the holder of the correct password read "wrong password". The new arm sits after the `signed_in` arm and before the password arm, keyed on the row's audience alone; it reads neither the caller's email claim nor the password, so no answer at this layer can differ by allowlist membership or by password correctness. Verified on the tree: the service refuses an unsatisfied audience before it reads or verifies any password, exactly as the arm's comment states.
- **The allowlisted-claim-without-the-right-password cells move from 401 to 404 — right, and the only defensible answer.** The audience is satisfied by the caller's own unverified claim (lowercased and matched against the stored list, bound to no identity), so an answer that kept the password arms for an allowlisted claim and gave the generic refusal to any other would be the membership oracle the card forbids. The cost — an allowlisted recipient loses the password hint and must send both together — is stated in the changeset and the PR's acceptance notes. This satisfies the card's ask (one refusal whatever password and whatever email were sent) and its ⛔ (no answer that differs by password correctness before the audience is satisfied); nothing answers by email, so by triage's own rule no `[Decision]` card is owed.
- **Placement and the untouched arms — right.** On the plugin mount the arm is inside the live-row block; on the dispatcher twin it is guarded by the same liveness predicate. So the standing-policy gate still answers first, a revoked or expired `email` link still reaches the 410 arm, and `public`, `link_only` and `signed_in` links keep their answers (the `signed_in` order from the sibling fix is unchanged). The audience contract has four values; the two the service gates on now both have a probe arm ahead of the password arm, and the other two do not gate, so no sibling shape of this defect remains at this door.
- **Equality with the generic refusal — right.** The arm calls the helper the unknown-token path already uses, so the refusal equals the unknown-token answer and the answer a password-less `email` link has always given; the three whole-answer pins (status, envelope and headers) hold both mounts to that on every refused cell.
- **No vocabulary change.** No error code is added or retired; the ledger and the route ledger are untouched; the auto-generated references still list the three codes. No hand-written doc or QA-checklist clause names the email-plus-password cell, and the clauses that name the email audience ("an off-list email is refused") remain true. Nothing goes stale.
- **Test surface.** The one table that holds both mounts gains the email dimension (14 rows, 3 pins); the fixture object now permits the `email` audience. The red-on-main, green-after and four ablation readings are the dev's and were not re-run here; the head's check-runs are the gate verdicts.

### ② Semver level

- **`@objectstack/plugin-sharing: patch`, `@objectstack/runtime: patch` — right.** Both are published packages (neither is private) and both change; a fix in a released package takes `patch`. No export is added, removed or renamed; `packages/spec` is untouched; no ledger code is added. `skip-changeset` would have been wrong and was not used. `Check Changeset` and the ADR-0087 registration gate (inside `Lint & Repo Gates`) are green.
- **`Clause-②: no`, no arm — right.** The question the value answers is whether the card widens an accept set or opens a surface: it does neither. The `(narrowing)` arm is owed when a published accept set or value domain shrinks; here no previously served request is refused, and no code leaves the door's vocabulary (the two 401 codes are still answered for the other audiences). What changes is which existing refusal an already-refused subset reads. This matches triage's "Lane, scope and Clause ② are unchanged" and the dispatch's declaration; the changeset body carries the same line and the consumer-facing sentence (send the email and the password together; the door no longer prompts first), which is what an upgrading SDK caller greps. The maintainer's p1 + `target:v18` class for a REST-door narrowing is a grading class and is already on the card; it does not by itself turn the arm, which is defined on the accept set.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev deviations, all three answered:

1. A depth-1 fetch of a pinned commit so a tooling self-test's positive control is readable: accepted — objects added to the shared store, no ref moved, no worktree affected.
2. The gate battery held the verify lock for about 18 minutes: accepted — the lane clause asked for the lock; the agent file's wording is a process note, no rule breached, nothing to re-run.
3. Commit trailers in the repo's model-free pair and the PR body in the session-URL footer form: correct — the repo instruction file is the source of truth and the pre-push hook refuses a model identifier; verified on all three branch commits.

`open_questions`: none declared, none found.

Out-of-scope findings, escalated to the owning seat (this review is read-only and posts one comment):

4. **The companion messages door — ESCALATED, a card is owed.** Verified by this reviewer's own read at the head: on the plugin mount that door passes only the password to the service's resolve gate (no signed-in identity, no email claim); on the dispatcher twin it passes the signed-in identity and the password (no email claim). So an `email`-audience link's companion route cannot resolve on either mount, and the two mounts diverge for a `signed_in` link. A different public door and a different fix; correctly left out of this PR. The seat files it with the dev-report's dedupe words. Not blocking.
5. **The audience is satisfied by an unverified claim — noted, escalated as a design note.** No contract text claims verification, and this property is precisely why the uniform refusal is the only non-oracle answer at this door. If the product ever wants a verified recipient, that is a `[Decision]` card, not a rider here.

Reviewer's own flags:

6. **Cost, not bytes (abstract).** The service's own gate answers its undifferentiated refusal before the password work when the audience is unsatisfied and after it when the audience is satisfied, so the two refusals are equal in bytes (pinned) but not necessarily in cost. Pre-existing in the service, untouched by this diff, and outside the card's ask, which is the answer code. The seat decides whether it is a card. Not blocking.
7. **Tier.** By the recogniser's file-list face this diff is the declaration face (no published schema, no governed path); the tier served here is the one the dispatch assigned under the lane's narrowing rule, as the claim records it.
8. **Disclosure.** The PR body and the changeset describe answer grids and codes and no reproduction recipe; this record keeps the same shape.
9. **Console behaviour** (the dev's statement that the console sends no email claim and builds no `email` audience) is consistent with the card body and affects the wording a dead-end link shows, not the accept set; the sibling repo is outside this review's inputs and was not read.
10. **Pin gap, minor.** No row pins a revoked or expired `email` link's 410; the liveness condition guarantees it structurally on both mounts. Not blocking.
11. **Governance and size.** No governed surface in the file list; 182 changed lines across 4 files, under the human-merge threshold.
12. **Check-runs, as read by this act (2026-10-14T11:56Z).** Green: `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Build Core`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Check Changeset`, every `Lint ·` and `Type Check ·` lane, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, the claim and single-writer guards. Pending: `Test Core` shards 1/6 through 6/6 were `in_progress`, and the aggregate `Test Core` context had not yet reported. Pending is pending, not red: the verdict below is on the diff; landing still waits for those conclusions to read `success`.
